facts.fact: Techhive Advisory says Ethiopia's Personal Data Protection Proclamation was published in the Federal Negarit Gazette on 24 July 2024, bringing it into effect, and that Articles 18-21 make international transfers depend on an Authority adequacy decision, explicit consent of the data subject, necessity, or public registry purposes, with sensitive data transfers needing the Authority's prior authorisation.

facts.fact: The law firm Haymanot & Advocates says Directive SBB/94/2025 makes transfers abroad of non-customer data by banks conditional on National Bank of Ethiopia prior written approval, disclosure of destinations, adequate protection in the receiving jurisdiction and service level agreements.

The same source says Proclamation No. 1321/2024 permits transfers of personal data abroad only where the receiving country gives appropriate protection, the person consents explicitly, or the authority approves in advance.
An Addis Ababa University thesis examines the conditions for cross-border transfer of data set out in the 2024 Personal Data Protection Proclamation.
